description: Hi! I am participating in the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge. Focusing on storytelling, presentation, and web design using AI tools.
summary:
Left Behind is an interactive 3D web experience that tells the story of eight historic rovers left on the Moon and Mars: Lunokhod 1 and 2, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity and Perseverance. Over half a century of exploration has left dozens of machines on other worlds, yet their histories are often buried in dry technical documents. Our project turns that data into a story people can scroll through, explore and play.

Visitors can rotate a 3D model of each rover and read its diary (retold from mission data), compare the real distances each one drove in an interactive chart, and see how the six-wheel rocker-bogie suspension keeps a rover level over rocks. They can then drive a rover across a 3D Moon-to-Mars landscape and collect eight signal beacons that unlock each diary. The experience is built with WebGL and Three.js and runs in any browser with no installation. By making space history playful, we hope to inspire students and keep these machines remembered.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Left Behind is a scroll-driven story and a 3D game about eight rovers that were left on the Moon and Mars: Lunokhod 1 and 2, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity and Perseverance. Visitors rotate a 3D model of each rover and read its diary, compare real driving distances in an interactive chart, explore how the rocker-bogie suspension works with a slider, and then drive a rover across a Moon-to-Mars landscape, collecting eight beacons that unlock the diaries.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Many of these machines are remembered only through technical reports. We turn mission data into a story that students and the public can explore in a few minutes, on any device, with no installation. Our aim is to keep the history of these rovers visible and to spark curiosity about robotic exploration.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Three.js (WebGL) for all 3D scenes. Rover models, planet textures and terrain are generated procedurally in code, so the page needs no external image or model files. Distances and dates come from NASA mission pages, including Perseverance passing Opportunity's total distance (45.22 km vs 45.16 km) on 11 October 2026.

CREATIVITY

Instead of a text article, the story is something you can touch: a garage of 3D rovers, a physics-style suspension demo, and a playable mission whose rewards are the rovers' own stories.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Accuracy of figures, clear labelling of reconstructed diary text, performance on phones (lighter models and on-screen controls), keyboard access, and reduced-motion support.
